subject: Request: One-time scaling credit + modified T&Cs for HealthOps pilot (VP/CFO signoff)
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@healthops.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot pricing ask + credit request — HealthOps enterprise pilot

Hi Daniel / team,

Thanks again for the demo on Friday — great signal from your engineering team about production timelines. As discussed, HealthOps is ready to move forward with a 6-month pilot but needs two commercial concessions to get legal and procurement comfortable: a one-time scaling credit to offset initial burst usage, and a short-term amendment to invoice cadence (net-60 to net-45) so payments align with their collections.

Proposed (customer-facing):
- One-time scaling credit equal to 12% of the estimated first three months' usage (applies to invoice(s) covering months 1–3).
- Pilot commitment: 100k generated tokens/month minimum for first 3 months (no carryover).
- Standard SLA; Redwood to provide dedicated onboarding support during ramp.

I attach the latest proposal (HOP-Enterprise-Proposal-v2.pdf) for your procurement team.

Before I send anything back to Procurement, I need internal approval on the credit level and confirmation that the credit and shorter invoice terms are acceptable to finance/legal. Can you confirm who I should loop in for VP/CFO signoff?

Thanks,
Nikhil
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: HOP-Enterprise-Proposal-v2.pdf (proposal)

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@healthops.com>

Thanks Nikhil — appreciate the fast follow.

The ask is reasonable on our side; procurement is specifically asking for (a) the credit to be applied up-front on the first invoice and (b) a clear expiration for the pilot price so we don’t default into a discounted rate after month 6. Can you provide a short memo describing the credit mechanics, the business justification, and the financial impact to Redwood? We will need that to present to our internal purchasing council.

If you can also include a DocuSign-ready amendment to the MSA that calls out net-45 and the credit, that would speed things up.

-Daniel
Director, Partnerships — HealthOps

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 08:41:10 -0700
Subject: RE: Pilot pricing ask + credit request — HealthOps enterprise pilot

Looping in legal and finance. Nikhil — good opportunity; we should move quickly but limit upside risk. See proposed internal exception terms below. Priyom / Marcus please review and sign off (Marcus: this is a VP/CFO approval ask).

Internal exception proposal (recommended):
- One-time scaling credit: 12% of invoiced usage for months 1–3, applied as a credit on month-1 invoice.
- Expiration: credit explicitly applies only to the pilot term; default post-pilot pricing reverts to list rates unless a new commitment is signed.
- Commit: minimum usage 100k tokens/month for months 1–3; if minimum not met, credit is clawed back pro rata on month-3 invoice.
- Invoice cadence: net-45 for pilot invoices only; revert to customer standard thereafter.
- Legal: include simple amendment language, no permanent changes to MSA, and no precedent-setting statements (explicit one-off).

Attached is a quick margin impact forecast (margin-impact-forecast-0901.xlsx) showing expected unit economics at 12% credit with the proposed commit. The net lifetime impact across the 6-month expected relationship is limited — this is a conversion prioritization tradeoff.

Asks:
- Marcus: sign off if acceptable from a finance P&L and cash flow perspective (we prefer net-45 to accelerate collection but I understand the trade).
- Priyom: confirm amendment language is clean and doesn't create ongoing liabilities.
- Aditya: if you can flag any channel/partner implications (reseller discounts, marketplace listings) that would be useful.

I’ll draft a short executive exception memo once we have Marcus/Priyom inputs and loop in Nik for the customer-facing DocuSign.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0120

Attachments: margin-impact-forecast-0901.xlsx (internal analysis)

Marcus — forwarding the thread and Marissa's recommendation. Per Marissa, we recommend approving a one-time 12% scaling credit (applied to month-1 invoice) with the commit and clawback language. Summary attached as an executive exception memo for signoff.

Executive ask (single line): Marcus Lin (CFO) approval to permit a one-time 12% credit applied to month-1 invoice, net-45 invoice cadence for pilot, and one-off MSA amendment limited to the pilot term.

Why approve:
- Customer is ready to convert to a paid pilot and is a strategic target in the health vertical; expected ARR expansion potential after pilot.
- Short-term margin impact (see attached) is manageable and offset by topline conversion.

1) Draft DocuSign amendment (Priyom/Legal) — I will send final for signature.

3) Sales playbook note to mark this as one-off exception.
